title: Notification System: Scalability and Trade-offs
description: Deep dive into scaling notification system. Explore advanced patterns, bottlenecks, and production-ready architectures.

data.text: Scale the notification system to handle millions of users. Address bottlenecks, optimize performance, and ensure high availability.

data.title: Scalability Patterns
data.code:
Scaling Strategies for Notification System:

Horizontal Scaling:
- Add more service instances
- Use load balancers
- Implement auto-scaling

Database Scaling:
- Read replicas for read-heavy workloads
- Database sharding by user/region
- Caching layers (Redis, CDN)

Caching Strategies:
- CDN for static assets
- Application cache (Redis)
- Database query cache

Message Queues:
- Decouple services with Kafka/RabbitMQ
- Handle async processing
- Event-driven architecture

Monitoring & Observability:
- Distributed tracing (Jaeger/Zipkin)
- Metrics (Prometheus/Grafana)
- Structured logging (ELK)

Fault Tolerance:
- Circuit breakers (Hystrix/Polly)
- Retries with exponential backoff
- Graceful degradation

data.title: Production Considerations
data.text: Real systems need: health checks, canary deployments, feature flags, A/B testing, disaster recovery, and capacity planning. Always document SLAs, SLOs, and error budgets.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Monitor everything with metrics and traces
Plan for failures with circuit breakers
data.takeaway: Scaling Notification System requires horizontal scaling, caching, message queues, and comprehensive monitoring. Every component should be replaceable and scalable independently.
